reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared patterns among misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations that may not be immediately apparent. This ensures both qualitative insight and quantitative validation of shared spurious features across all instances.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 6097) and assess whether any of these features are semantically related to class outcomes.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: List of shared features and their semantic plausibility as predictors of income class

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared features (like 'Married-civ-spouse' or 'Husband') might act as spurious correlations—indirectly influencing predictions due to demographic bias or data leakage instead of true causal relevance.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Insight into whether a shared feature is spurious or semantically meaningful

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides consistent, interpretable feature attributions across instances, enabling detection of shared high-importance features. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local explanations to validate the model's reliance on certain features. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature changes predictions significantly, helping to isolate spurious dependencies. Together, these tools validate and reinforce autonomous observations about shared spurious patterns.
